name: Freshwater fish (tilapia, catfish, trout, carp)
scope_note: Freshwater finfish (tilapia, catfish, trout, carp), fresh or frozen, edible portion. Lead binds Fiji 200; total mercury binds the EU lower-mercury 300 ceiling (conservative subcategory-wide selection). MeHg bounded by tHg; total Cr binds HK fish 1000; Ni/Al screened; Sn/Cr-VI not-material. Canned product routes to the canned-seafood subcategory.

Pb.basis: edible portion, wet weight. Fiji FSR 2009 muscle-meat-of-fish Pb 200 is the strictest sovereign (EU general fish-muscle 300 concurs).

Cd.basis: edible portion, wet weight; general fish-muscle cadmium 50.

tAs.basis: edible portion, wet weight; total arsenic 1000 (Singapore/Paraguay/Israel).

iAs.basis: edible portion, wet weight; inorganic arsenic 100 (EU 2025/1891; HK Cap 132V).

tHg.basis: edible portion, wet weight; total mercury. Trout is an EU 2023/915 listed lower-mercury species (300); the freshwater subcategory is held to the 300 ceiling as the consumer-protective bound covering the whole subcategory (tilapia/catfish/carp are not individually EU-listed and would otherwise fall to the general 500 — 300 is the stricter, conservative selection).

MeHg.rationale: Methylmercury is bounded by total mercury (MeHg <= tHg). The binding total-mercury ceiling (300) is stricter than the lowest applicable sovereign methylmercury ML for freshwater fish (general fish MeHg 500), so passing tHg guarantees MeHg compliance; no separate methylmercury ceiling is published. Audit-affirmed (2026-08-14).
MeHg.reference_method: Total-mercury screen; reflex MeHg speciation cannot exceed the tHg ceiling.
MeHg.regulatory_basis: Bounded by the total-Hg lower-mercury-fish ceiling (EU 2023/915, 300); no sovereign MeHg ML sits below it
MeHg.jurisdictions_checked: EU; US-FDA; MX; PH; TT; TH; HK

Ni.rationale: No jurisdiction sets a nickel ML for fish (EU 2024/1987 nickel is plant-food/seaweed only). Screened rather than assigned a mis-based number.
Ni.reference_method: Total-nickel screen (ICP-MS); no sovereign fish Ni ML.
Ni.trigger: periodic nickel screen; flag on anomalous elevation

Sn.rationale: Fresh/frozen freshwater fish has no tinplate contact; tin is a can-migration analyte and no sovereign sets a non-canned fish tin matrix limit (audit-affirmed). If canned, certified under the canned-seafood subcategory.
Sn.reference_method: Packaging control (non-tinplate); ICP-MS per-lot screen; escalate to canned-seafood Sn if tinplate-packed.
Sn.regulatory_basis: No non-canned fish Sn ML; canned-seafood Sn limits are can-only
Sn.jurisdictions_checked: Codex CXS 193; EU; US-FDA; MX; CR; HK

Al.rationale: No credible regulator sets an aluminium contaminant ML for seafood; aluminium in fish is background, managed by intake vs the EFSA/JECFA TWI.
Al.reference_method: Total-aluminium screen (ICP-MS); managed by TWI; no per-food seafood contaminant ML.
Al.trigger: periodic aluminium screen; flag on anomalous elevation

Cr.basis: edible portion, wet weight; total chromium 1000 (HK Cap 132V fish).

Cr-VI.rationale: Cr-VI is bounded by the total-chromium government limit (HK fish 1000); no Cr-VI food ML exists and Cr(VI) is reduced to Cr(III) in a reducing animal-tissue matrix. Rebuttable if a routed source reports hexavalent chromium in fish.
Cr-VI.reference_method: Bounded by total-chromium government limit; reflex Cr-VI speciation only on anomalously elevated total chromium.
Cr-VI.regulatory_basis: No Cr-VI food ML anywhere; bounded by total chromium (HK fish 1000)
Cr-VI.jurisdictions_checked: EU; Codex; US-FDA; HK; EPA (water only)

method: HMTc Method v2.0 (government-limit default; explicit-id lookup; MeHg speciation-bounded by tHg on animal seafood; seaweed on dry-matter basis)
